status: PROPOSED. Authored alongside the v1.0.0 cases, not yet implemented. The implementation must READ this file rather than hard-coding terms in Python, or the keyword_list_sha in manifest.json is meaningless.

matching.apostrophe_normalisation: U+2019 and U+02BC are folded to ASCII apostrophe before matching, because Bangladeshi resumes mix both and 'women's' must not match 'women’s' by accident of typography.
matching.note: Plain substring matching. No word-boundary logic in v1.0.0 -- the excluded list below explains why most broad words are out, and why the narrow phrases in this file do not need boundaries.

deliberately_excluded.reason: Bare 'women's' flags a candidate who co-founded a women's rights reading group or worked at an NGO. That is advocacy experience, not a credential signalling gender. The gendered-organisation PHRASES are listed individually instead.
A legitimate job requirement, not a signal about a candidate. This pass scans candidate-derived text; the job's own requirements live in the job, not the resume.

Collides with 'recent graduate programme', an ordinary job and course description. The real age proxy here is graduation YEAR, not the phrase. Deferred to v1.0.1 as a date-proximity rule rather than kept as a substring.
Bare 'male' appears in 'male-dominated field', which is a candidate describing a problem, not a credential. The credential case ('young male preferred') is listed as a phrase.
Same reasoning as 'male', and it collides with 'female candidates preferred', which is job text.
Far too broad to be a useful proxy; would flag most of the corpus.

known_limitations.limitation: There is NO numeric age detection. A line reading '22 years old' is not caught by any term in this list.
known_limitations.why_it_matters: A stated age is a stronger proxy than 'young and energetic', and it is the more common form in the resumes this product will ingest.
known_limitations.planned: v1.0.1 — a regex rule over explicit age and date-of-birth phrasings, with its own category (11) and its own false-positive cases.

known_limitations.limitation: There is NO graduation-year proximity rule, so a 1994 graduate and a 2026 graduate score identically.
known_limitations.why_it_matters: This is the mechanism behind the 2018 proxy case. 'Recent graduate' was removed from the term list because of a false-positive collision, and nothing replaced it yet.
known_limitations.planned: v1.0.1 — compare graduation year against a role's stated window, applied at ranking time rather than as a keyword.

known_limitations.limitation: The list holds English phrases only. A Bengali-language resume can carry every one of these signals in transliterated or Bengali script and none will be caught.
known_limitations.why_it_matters: The primary market is Bangladesh. A pass that only reads English will report clean on exactly the population the product is for.
known_limitations.planned: v1.1.0 — Bengali term list, authored with native review rather than machine translation.

known_limitations.limitation: Substring matching has no word boundaries, so a term can match inside a longer word.
known_limitations.why_it_matters: Low today, because the terms are multi-word, but it becomes a real risk if a single short term is ever added.
known_limitations.planned: Revisit if any single-word term is added.

known_limitations.limitation: Single-word vague and age-coded words are absent by choice. 'Energetic', 'articulate', 'mature', 'ambitious', 'young', 'dynamic' and 'passive' are NOT terms.
known_limitations.why_it_matters: A rationale reading 'Energetic and culturally aligned' is age-coded and would NOT be flagged by v1.0.0. This was found while authoring RAT-010, which originally carried that exact wording.
known_limitations.why_not_just_added: Each of these is a common positive word in ordinary professional text. Adding them bare would flag ordinary CVs and rationales, and the 0-false-positive criterion in Arch Doc 7.4.5 is not negotiable. 'Energetic' is the sharpest example: on its own it is an adjective, not a proxy.
known_limitations.how_it_is_handled: The gap is recorded rather than papered over. The case was reworded to carry a term that IS in the list, so v1.0.0 measures what it claims to measure, and this limitation stays visible for v1.0.1 to solve properly -- plausibly by scoring vague adjectives in the rationale GENERATION step, where the full sentence is available, rather than by substring-matching single words in a free-text pass.
